title: Select Works of Porphyry
author: Porphyry (Taylor trans)
description: Select Works of Porphyry, translated from the Greek by Thomas Taylor (London, 1823), with an appendix explaining the allegory of the wanderings of Ulysses. Porphyry of Tyre (c. 234-305 CE), disciple and biographer of Plotinus and editor of the Enneads, was a leading Neoplatonist philosopher. The volume contains On Abstinence from Animal Food, in four books, a philosophical defence of vegetarianism grounded in the kinship of all living beings, the purity of the soul and the religious customs of Egypt, Persia, India and the Pythagoreans; the Auxiliaries to the Perception of Intelligible Natures (Sententiae), concise propositions on the incorporeal and the soul's ascent; and the essay on the Cave of the Nymphs in Homer's Odyssey, a classic of allegorical interpretation reading the cave as an image of the cosmos and the soul's descent into generation. It is valuable for Neoplatonic ethics, symbolism and myth interpretation.
